messages:
maria: Heads-up — getting flagged invoices for March where the same client_id shows up under two different orgs after an API key rotation. Looks like replayed requests from the fallback path are being attributed to the old org. Anyone else seeing this?
jonathan: Yup, noticed it earlier. Replays from the fallback proxy preserve the original X-Client-Id header and we currently prioritize that over api_key mapping at ingest.
sam: Current ingest dedupe window is 10s. These replays happen ~20-40s later so they bypass dedupe and get counted again.
elaine: Can we dedupe on a request-level fingerprint instead? SDKs aren't consistently populating request_id on streaming fallbacks though.
jonathan: Request_id is only reliably present at finalization. Streaming token events come in without it, so switching fully to request_id would miss token fragments.
maria: What if we defer dedupe to the billing join stage and resolve attribution there (pick the most authoritative mapping)? Pros/cons?
sam: Billing-join dedupe would solve attribution but requires keeping raw events much longer and pushes complexity into invoice generation. We also lose early-rate limiting signals.
metering-bot: ingest: detected 1234 events in rotation-window (2026-03-18T10:12Z). Potential duplicates flagged: 98. sample: client=abc123 old_org=redwood-dev new_org=redwood-prod
elaine: Proposed compromise: emit api_key_hash from edge for every request, then at ingest prefer api_key_hash->org when present. Also add a rotation flag at edge when we see an API key rotate for that client.
jonathan: Edge change is doable but needs a rollout flag. For safety, expose a Console toggle "billing-relaxed-mode" during canaries so we don't accidentally reattribute production traffic mid-rollout.
maria: Migration plan idea: 1) augment events at edge with api_key_hash, 2) change ingest dedupe priority to prefer api_key_hash when mapping exists, 3) run a backfill for impacted window and surface a reconciliation report in Console.
sam: Backfill estimate: ~12 CPU-hours + heavy S3 IO. Also we should figure legal/billing policy before touching historical invoices.
ops-ci: Legal says invoice changes require customer opt-in and full audit trail. We can add a reconciliation column in the Console and an opt-in flow to reissue corrected invoices.
elaine: Quick query to surface dup candidates (may miss streaming partials): ```sql
SELECT api_key_hash, session_fingerprint, count(*) as hits
FROM metering.raw_events
WHERE timestamp >= '2026-03-01' and timestamp < '2026-04-01'
GROUP BY 1,2
HAVING hits > 1
ORDER BY hits DESC
LIMIT 100;
```
maria: Nice. Can someone run that and attach a sample to the RFC? I'll draft the RFC and loop in billing/legal/ops. Short term: add a Console metric "suspected-rotation-duplicates" per-account and an export for accounts with >10 suspected hits so Billing can reach out. :thinking:
jonathan: I can add the edge header and flag rollout plan. Sam can scope the backfill job. Elaine — can you own the Console metric and reconciliation UI?
elaine: Yep — I'll spin up a small dashboard with per-account counts and a link to sample events. Also will include an action to request a manual review.
sam: I'll put together backfill numbers and a rough runbook. If legal requires opt-in, we'll coordinate Messaging.
maria: Thanks all — RFC by EOD tomorrow. If we can get the edge change behind a rollout flag this week, we can reduce new duplicates ASAP.
notes: thread about client_id rotation causing cross-org attribution; debate ingest vs billing-join dedupe, edge header fix, console UX for reconciliation and legal implications
